races.name: North Wales Business Day Novices' Hurdle Race (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Hoe Joly Smoke
runners_data.note: Confirmed lead horse for Dan Skelton (9/21 in 14 days) ridden by Harry Skelton; Good-ground record shows 4 runs with 1W3P and returns after 114 days, but the STYLE_FIT tag reminds that if this race shape doesn't allow him to control from the front, his chance is tempered — here, however, he should get his position unchallenged.

runners_data.name: Sovereignlightcafe
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's five-year-old returns from a 251-day absence with a form string of 38- and zero wins or places on Good ground across six attempts; his natural role is as a hold-up horse running from the back, and the midfield map position overstates how far forward he will actually race in this low-tempo scenario.

runners_data.name: Iamyouare
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's six-year-old carries amateur claimer Mr Harry Brown (10lb) but has solid Good-ground form (1W3P in six runs) at distances around 2m-2m3f, sits prominently, and is the most likely horse to inherit or challenge the lead if Hoe Joly Smoke weakens — the trainer's 0/10 in the 14-day window is a minor flag.

runners_data.name: That Old Chestnut
runners_data.note: Henry Daly's six-year-old has only two recorded Good-ground runs with finishes of 10th and 8th, has been off 119 days, and carries a clear fade warning that undermines any scenario in which he needs to produce a sustained late effort — David Bass's presence is the one positive angle.

runners_data.name: Whinny Houston
runners_data.note: Sheila Lewis's five-year-old has run just 16 days ago and returned finishes of 13th and 11th on Good in recent outings; the fade warning and a P0-0 recent form string make this a horse to oppose rather than support in any finishing-speed scenario, regardless of position in the race.

races.paceDynamic: Hoe Joly Smoke is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over 2m3½f on Good ground at Bangor. Iamyouare is a prominent racer who will push forward early and sit just behind Hoe Joly Smoke, giving the pace some shape but not threatening to overheat it. The three hold-up types — Sovereignlightcafe, That Old Chestnut, and Whinny Houston — will track from further back, though both That Old Chestnut and Whinny Houston carry a fade warning that severely limits their finishing threat. This race shape is a classic setup for a prominent or front-running horse to control and conserve energy before stretching rivals in the home straight — the profile that benefits most clearly is the prominent-to-lead racer who can dictate without being pressured. The field holds more hold-up types than can meaningfully deliver from that position given the steady gallop: Sovereignlightcafe is a true hold-up horse mapped closer than natural, and in a slow-tempo scenario the margin for late closers is narrow.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hoe Joly Smoke Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Hoe Joly Smoke bowls along unchallenged and sets a steady, controlled tempo that suits a front-running hold on the race.
scenarios.body: Hoe Joly Smoke travels comfortably on Good ground at a pace of his own choosing, and with no one willing to press him, he simply extends his advantage from the last few hurdles; the Skelton team's 9/21 14-day strike rate adds confidence to this well-managed front-running role. Prominent types who can latch on early are the primary beneficiaries, and Iamyouare is positioned to inherit should Hoe Joly Smoke tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Iamyouare Picks Up Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Hoe Joly Smoke fades after setting the pace and Iamyouare, sitting prominently throughout, sweeps past to win.
scenarios.body: Iamyouare has Good-ground course form (1W3P in similar conditions across 6 runs) and is well-placed by Mr Harry Brown to capitalise on any weakness from the leader in the closing stages. Having sat just off the pace for the entire race, Iamyouare would be fresher than Hoe Joly Smoke at the last and could pick up cleanly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses sharply late on and genuine hold-up horses find enough energy to finish past tiring leaders.
scenarios.body: Sovereignlightcafe is a true hold-up type but arrives on 251 days off and has no Good-ground wins in six attempts, making this scenario dependent on a significant pace collapse rather than natural late momentum. That Old Chestnut and Whinny Houston both carry fade warnings that make them unreliable in any scenario requiring a sustained finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy No True Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the race fragments, the pace collapses mid-race, and the field strings out with no runner able to assert authority.
scenarios.body: With fading hold-up types making up the majority of this small field, a scenario where no runner travels smoothly is plausible only if conditions deteriorate or jumping errors disrupt order. Even then, Hoe Joly Smoke and Iamyouare are better positioned than the hold-up trio to scavenge a result from chaos.

watchPoints.text: Watch Hoe Joly Smoke's jumping — if he makes errors early at Bangor's tight track, Iamyouare is perfectly placed to seize the initiative and the entire pace map flips.

Sovereignlightcafe returns from 251 days off with no Good-ground form; if the yard has done their work quietly, a market move late would be significant given the hold-up horse redistribution underplays his true drawn back position.

Both That Old Chestnut and Whinny Houston carry fade warnings — if they move up to challenge at the top of the straight, watch for them stopping quickly and causing interference with horses behind them.

The controlled pace set by Hoe Joly Smoke means the race is likely to quicken only once turning for home — horses who have been travelling comfortably in prominent positions will have a meaningful advantage over those who need a strong gallop to make headway.

Iamyouare's amateur rider Mr Harry Brown takes 10lbs — monitor whether he settles the horse cleanly in the early stages, as a prominent horse that pulls or over-races into a steady Hoe Joly Smoke-led tempo will have less left for the finish.

races.name: Genesis Wealth Management Novices' Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Soldier In Mayo
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner whose entire tactical advantage rests on being allowed to dictate unchallenged; returns from a 475-day absence which is the key fitness query, though his two good-ground wins from five sim-going runs suggest conditions are ideal if he strips fit.|

runners_data.name: My Bobby's Lass
runners_data.note: Boasts an excellent record on good ground (8/10 sim-going, 2W3P), won twice over 20f trips and is a genuine stayer, but the 436-day layoff under a tongue-tie is a serious concern and Charlie Deutsch will need to nurse her into the race from her natural hold-up position.|

runners_data.name: Barry Fife
runners_data.note: Had a run just 16 days ago which keeps him sharp, and his three placed efforts from six good-ground starts show he handles the going; his form string of P37 and 3 consecutive placed efforts suggests consistent jumping without winning — he needs others to capitulate.|

runners_data.name: Moonlightinthepark
runners_data.note: Greenall/Guerriero have a runner in form (T14 1/7) and the tongue-tie is retained, but a sequence of 6796P on recent form is difficult to ignore — naturally a hold-up horse whose sim-going record of 0W0P in 6 attempts makes this trip a stern test of belief.|

runners_data.name: Rule Me In
runners_data.note: Has run seven times on good or similar ground without winning (0W0P, 3/10 placed), and his hold-up style needs a stiff pace to produce his best — with Soldier In Mayo likely to control rather than force the tempo, Jack Tudor faces a tactical headache.|

runners_data.name: Hiero Sport
runners_data.note: Recent run 16 days ago keeps him fresh and he has winning form to his name (2W in 13 sim-going starts), but the hurdle headgear (tongue-tie/hood) signals past behavioural issues; natural hold-up style means Jonathan Burke will likely be further back than ideal in this shape.|

runners_data.name: Rockvale
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse who showed ability when second over 21f on good ground but has fallen or pulled up in two of six recent starts, suggesting jumping reliability is a concern; the big weight concession (22lbs to the top weights) is an asset on paper but consistent form is lacking.|

runners_data.name: Delgany Second Now
runners_data.note: The Skelton yard's formidable T14 stats (9/21) and Harry Skelton's booking are the headline here — this 4-year-old has won two of five on good ground and his last three runs show a progressive 7-7-5-1-1 arc; naturally a hold-up type who will need to be produced late but has the class to do so.|

races.paceDynamic: Soldier In Mayo is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 8-runner novices' handicap chase over 2m4½f on good ground at Bangor, and with no rival likely to press him hard from the outset, he is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop throughout. The pace is unlikely to be severe — Soldier In Mayo's record suggests he is most effective when allowed to bowl along at his own rhythm rather than being wound up by competition, and nothing in this field has the profile or mandate to challenge him for the lead. Behind him, the remaining seven runners are almost entirely hold-up types by nature, meaning the midfield and rear will be congested and the race will essentially be a lone-leader contest rather than a true test of stamina at a fierce tempo. This race shape strongly favours a horse that can either lead and sustain it (Soldier In Mayo) or travel well just off the pace and produce a clean, well-timed challenge; genuine hold-up horses that need a searching gallop to bring them into play are at a structural disadvantage here. The field holds more hold-up types than can all settle naturally at the rear — Delgany Second Now, Hiero Sport and Rule Me In are among those most likely to be manoeuvred closer to the pace than their natural style demands.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solo leader controls
scenarios.trigger: If Soldier In Mayo is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and sets a controlled gallop that suits his jumping rhythm.
scenarios.body: Soldier In Mayo dictates from the front on his favoured good ground, bowls along at a sustainable clip and his rivals, trapped in a congested hold-up pack, struggle to close the deficit in time over a trip that rewards front-runners when the pace is honest but not punishing. A clean round of jumping seals it, and the hold-up horses who need a stronger tempo to pick up never get the race they want.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer reels him in
scenarios.trigger: If Soldier In Mayo's jumping or stamina frays late and one of the hold-up types makes sustained progress from the final fence.
scenarios.body: Delgany Second Now, reunited with Harry Skelton and in hot form having won two of his last three on good ground, is best placed to mount a late challenge if the leader tires — his trainer Dan Skelton is in a rich vein at T14 (9/21) and the horse's recent course of form suggests he handles this trip well. My Bobby's Lass, who has a strong record on good ground (8/10 sim-going) and boasts two wins over identical trips, is the other credible finisher if the race opens up late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front runner falls away
scenarios.trigger: If Soldier In Mayo makes a jumping error or blows up on his return from 475 days off the track and the pace collapses.
scenarios.body: The lengthy absence is a genuine flag — Soldier In Mayo has not run since April 2024 and, while he showed ability before, a horse returning cold from 15+ months off may not be race-fit enough to sustain the lead over 2m4½f of fences on good ground. If he cries enough early on the home turn, Hiero Sport (two wins from 13 runs on sim-going, recent run 16 days ago) and Barry Fife (ran 16 days ago, placed last three completed starts on good ground) are freshest and best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-up cavalry arrives
scenarios.trigger: If the pace turns genuinely strong and the true hold-up horses are able to produce their best finish from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires conditions that this race shape is unlikely to generate — with one lone front-runner setting a measured tempo, the back-markers face too much to do and the structural disadvantage of being pushed wide or forced to race out of role in a compressed midfield. Rule Me In and Rockvale are the most naturally suited to this shape but their recent form (0W0P on sim-going for both) gives little confidence even if it does materialise.

watchPoints.text: Soldier In Mayo's jumping must be monitored from the first fence — a 475-day absence in a front-runner attempting 17 fences makes any early blunder potentially race-ending and would completely reshape the tactical picture.

Delgany Second Now bears close watching in the market — a 7-day turnaround with Harry Skelton booked and a trainer firing at 9/21 over 14 days is not a combination to dismiss, and any significant shortening suggests stable confidence is high.

My Bobby's Lass and Hiero Sport are both returning from significant breaks (436 and 16 days respectively) with headgear in place — watch whether either settles cleanly early, as jumping errors from hold-up horses in a compressed pack can cause interference.

With six of eight runners naturally inclined to race towards the rear, watch for crowding and traffic problems on the final bend at Bangor — horses wide on the track at that point tend to give ground, and those who find a clear run on the inner are at a premium.|

races.name: Goffs Yorton Sale 10th September Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Sure Touch
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up performer for Olly Murphy who handles Good ground well (9/15 sim-going, 3 wins) and whose last win came over 22f at a similar trip; 40 days off is not a concern for this yard but a slow pace will blunt his late challenge significantly.

runners_data.name: Tamarind Bay
runners_data.note: James Bowen partners a six-year-old in excellent recent form (two wins from last four completed runs) for Mickey Bowen, travelling well on Good ground and likely to sit a close second to Presentandcounting; a 20-day turnaround is a positive freshness angle.

runners_data.name: Homme Public
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor rides a nine-year-old whose recent form reads 0P-305 — inconsistent and winless on this going profile (0 wins from 7 sim-going runs) — making him the most vulnerable of the hold-up types if the pace is modest and prominent horses dominate the home straight; headgear (tongue-tie) noted but not transformative here.

runners_data.name: Regal Renaissance
runners_data.note: Ben Jones partners a lightly-framed eight-year-old whose form is outstanding (three wins from last five, all on Good or similar), travels prominently and jumps cleanly; 44 days since last run is the only mild query, though Jack Jones's yard is 2/12 in the last fortnight suggesting stable form is functional rather than flying.

runners_data.name: Presentandcounting
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner whose task is to set a fair 3m gallop for Donald McCain; the 12-year-old has an exceptional sim-going record (14/15) which speaks to jumping reliability on Good, but 53 days off and a modest OR of 115 mean rivals will not fear his finishing kick if he is collared late; Theo Gillard's claiming allowance helps offset the weight.

runners_data.name: Thickthorn Tom
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's six-year-old carries a remarkable recent sequence (four wins from five, all on Good-type ground) and is naturally a front-running or close-prominent type — placed into midfield on the map only because the race shape cannot house all hold-up horses at the rear; Harry Skelton's tactical intelligence could yet see him race far closer to the pace than his mapped slot implies, and that positional compromise tempers confidence in his chance landing from an orthodox hold-up berth.

races.paceDynamic: Presentandcounting is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no rival likely to seriously press for the lead over 3m on Good ground at Bangor, he should dictate a controlled, measured gallop from the outset — a tempo that suits his stamina-first profile rather than burning off rivals early. Tamarind Bay and Regal Renaissance are the prominent types who will look to track closely in second and third, meaning the early order is relatively settled and the pace should be honest but not frantic. Sure Touch and Homme Public operate from hold-up positions and will need the gallop to lift in the final circuit to maximise their late runs. This field holds more hold-up types than can naturally settle at the rear — Thickthorn Tom is a genuine front-running/prominent type who has been mapped to midfield because the race shape cannot accommodate all hold-up horses, and he is likely to race considerably closer to the pace than his mapped position suggests. A steady-to-fair gallop set by one unchallenged front-runner strongly favours the prominent racers who can track economically and pounce in the straight, with Tamarind Bay and Regal Renaissance best positioned to exploit that shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Presentandcounting Controls, Prominents Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Presentandcounting sets a sustainable gallop and no rival forces a pace increase, the prominent trackers inherit the advantage.
scenarios.body: Tamarind Bay and Regal Renaissance travel economically just off the leader and have the fitness and recent form to pick him off at the final fence, with the steady tempo suiting their jumping-and-travelling style over this 3m trip. Good ground, which both handle well per their sim-going records, means they can sustain momentum through the home straight without the race turning into a stamina test that might expose them.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Ups Arrive Too Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop remains conservative throughout and the prominent pair dominate from the front, the hold-up horses find the contest over before they can deliver their challenge.
scenarios.body: Sure Touch stays on under Lewis Saunders from the rear but the gap left by a slow tempo is too small to bridge in time, with Homme Public similarly disadvantaged by a lack of early pace to run into. The 3m trip at Bangor does not demand the searching gallop that true hold-up horses need, and prominent racers maintain their advantage to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Presentandcounting's 53-day absence tells and he weakens dramatically after setting the pace, creating a messy scramble up the home straight.
scenarios.body: Sure Touch, with the best sim-going record on this ground (9/15, 3 wins), is the most likely beneficiary if the front end collapses and a strong late run is rewarded. Homme Public has course-and-distance experience to capitalise but his inconsistent recent form (0P-305) makes him an unreliable vehicle for this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Thickthorn Tom Front Boot
scenarios.trigger: If Thickthorn Tom, a natural front-running type with a 4-wins-from-6 recent record, pushes forward from what is an artificially mapped midfield position and challenges for the lead early.
scenarios.body: This would disrupt Presentandcounting's rhythm and turn the race into a genuine test of stamina and jumping accuracy, potentially opening the door for his in-form profile to dominate — but racing out of his mapped role in this field shape reduces the probability materially. His style-fit score of 0.93 signals a real positional challenge, and the Skelton team may instead instruct a patient ride that leaves him chasing a race already controlled by others.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Thickthorn Tom — a horse who habitually races at the front — accepts a midfield position under Harry Skelton or pushes forward to challenge Presentandcounting for the lead, as this single decision reshapes the entire pace picture.

Monitor Presentandcounting's jumping in the early stages; a 53-day absence in a 12-year-old raises the risk of a jumping error or a fading run in the final mile that collapses the pace structure entirely.

Tamarind Bay's jumping accuracy at pace on Good ground is the key variable for the prominent-racer scenario — any fence mistake in the back straight will allow Regal Renaissance to move into the prime tracking position.

Sure Touch's rider Lewis Saunders claims 5lb, which is meaningful over 3m in a competitive handicap; watch whether he times the hold-up run correctly or gets outpaced when the prominent pair quicken at the third-last.

Regal Renaissance's trainer Jack Jones is 2/12 in the last 14 days — not a poor strike-rate, but worth monitoring in the market to confirm the horse is travelling to Bangor in the same form that delivered three wins from five recent starts.

races.name: Du Construction Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Ernest Gray
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner with a solid Good-going record (2W4P in 15 similar-going runs) and strong course fitness at OR 122, but recent form (166-42) shows inconsistency and he has lost his lead position before; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.91) is a minor flag given he IS the natural front runner here, but class rivals like Kiwi de Cotte may not let him coast.|

runners_data.name: Roger Pol
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up horse (hg:tb — tongue tie and blinkers) with a fair record on Good but struggled markedly in recent starts (17-698), and apprentice Isabelle Ryder (5lb claim) faces a stiff task coaxing a response after 40 days off; the trip (2m7f) is longer than most of his sim-going efforts but one win came over 24f.|

runners_data.name: Secret Trix
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's 9-year-old is a consistent placer — four runner-up or third-place finishes in the last five outings — with a tongue piece and hood, and she arrives 54 days fresh; her Good-going profile (11/15, 1W8P) suggests she stays involved late but rarely finds the extra to win, making her a likely place rather than a winning proposition.|

runners_data.name: Kiwi de Cotte
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced 6-year-old for Dan Skelton who carries a crisp form line (1-P131), two wins from four completed runs, all on Good ground; Harry Skelton's booking for a yard firing at T14:9/21 is a significant flag, and OR 117 leaves him with the most upside in this field on a track that suits prominent racing.|

runners_data.name: Speed Davis
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's 8-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse (two recent wins came from off the pace) but has been mapped to midfield because the rear of this field is congested; his T14 record (0/10) provides no encouragement and 54 days off combined with a modest OR 114 and no headgear adjustment make him hard to support in this configuration.|

races.paceDynamic: Ernest Gray and Kiwi de Cotte are the two confirmed prominent-to-front-running types in this five-runner field, and with Ernest Gray the sole confirmed front runner, he is almost certain to dictate from the front at a pace he controls over 2m7f on Good ground at Bangor. Kiwi de Cotte (Harry Skelton, Dan Skelton yard in strong form at T14:9/21) will push forward to contest the early lead or sit a close second, creating a pressured but sustainable gallop rather than a dawdle — this is not a race where the front will go unchallenged. Roger Pol, Secret Trix, and Speed Davis (the true hold-up types) will be ridden from off the pace, though Speed Davis has been redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is already occupied by two genuine closers and Speed Davis is unlikely to find his natural position at the back. The race shape — a genuine, competitive gallop set by Ernest Gray with Kiwi de Cotte breathing down his neck — strongly favours prominent racers who can travel into the tempo and idle rivals who stay involved, while pure hold-up horses face a stern test of whether the leaders leave enough to chase down from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ernest Gray Dictates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Ernest Gray leads unchallenged or Kiwi de Cotte fails to apply pressure and the front duo run a true but controlled gallop.
scenarios.body: Ernest Gray sets a sustainable pace over the long 2m7f trip on Good ground, building a lead that tests the hold-up horses' ability to close; Kiwi de Cotte, travelling prominently with Harry Skelton, is best placed to pounce if Ernest Gray tires late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Skelton Delivers Kiwi Late
scenarios.trigger: If Kiwi de Cotte tracks Ernest Gray patiently and Harry Skelton times a decisive run from two out.
scenarios.body: Kiwi de Cotte's recent form (1-P131, two wins in last four) and strong Skelton booking suggest a horse near the top of his game; travelling prominently on a track where the pace is honest, he can pick up Ernest Gray at the business end.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves too strong and the prominent horses empty, allowing the hold-up horses to swoop late.
scenarios.body: Secret Trix's model of consistent placed form (2-2-3-3 in last four) suggests she is best equipped to finish strongly if conditions suit a late run; Roger Pol has the class (1/24f/GOO in profile) to close ground on a tiring front pair.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Tactical Race
scenarios.trigger: If early pace collapses into a muddling affair with no horse willing to go on, producing a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A slow early tempo over this long trip would compress the field and negate hold-up horses' ability to pick up momentum; Kiwi de Cotte's tactical versatility and Ernest Gray's experience give them an edge in a contested sprint finish, but the pace data makes this scenario unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Ernest Gray's jumping must be monitored — if he makes a significant error at an early hurdle, Kiwi de Cotte (Harry Skelton) will immediately move to the front and fundamentally change the race shape.

Kiwi de Cotte's jumping under pressure from Ernest Gray at the final two flights is the critical contest — Dan Skelton runners T14:9/21 suggest confidence, but a novicey jump at the last could cost him if Ernest Gray is still upright.

Roger Pol's starting position and early behaviour behind the pace should be tracked — if Isabelle Ryder cannot hold him up early over this long 2m7f trip, his hold-up profile becomes redundant and his stamina reserves will be burned before the straight.

Secret Trix's consistency at placed level (four places in last five) means she is a credible each-way participant if the front pair tire, but watch whether Tom Hutsby (10lb claim) can manoeuvre her into the correct position turning for home, as her pattern relies on a clean passage through the field.

The Going is Good throughout the card at Bangor with no deterioration reported — no runner carries a going concern flag, so surface conditions are unlikely to produce any surprise, but the consistent Good surface may slightly favour horses with proven records on that ground such as Ernest Gray and Kiwi de Cotte over those with smaller Good-ground samples.

races.name: Kinsey Anniversary Mares' Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Jammy Jay
runners_data.note: Settled hold-up mare who has finished second on good going over the same trip-band and brings the class of an OR-98 rating into a relatively moderate field; 42 days off is within normal range, and Ben Poste has a competent book, but she needs others to soften things up ahead of her.

runners_data.name: I Heard A Rumour
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's lightly raced five-year-old returns from 171 days off for a yard in strong form (9/21 over 14 days), though her last three runs include a fall and two mid-pack finishes on softer ground; she is a genuine rear-runner in terms of race tactics but has been slotted into midfield on the map because there is no further room at the back — do not read her map position as her natural operating zone.

runners_data.name: Prettylady
runners_data.note: Two wins from her last four completed starts at this trip on good ground make her the most in-form runner in the field; Jack Tudor and the Greenall-Guerriero yard contribute solid credentials, tongue tie is fitted, and although she habitually settles off the pace she has enough acceleration to be a real factor from a handy position.

runners_data.name: Daring To Dream
runners_data.note: Harriet Dickin's mare carries hood and tongue tie and has shown a consistent midfield-to-rear pattern in her last five starts; her true inclination is to race further back than the pace map shows, and with OR-83 and a claiming partner (Megan Bevan 7lb) she needs things to go exactly right to land a blow — trainer sends only two runners in the 14-day window (0 wins).

runners_data.name: Northern Rose
runners_data.note: Gary Hanmer's mare is a genuine front runner with an outstanding record on good ground (15 runs, all good, 1W 8P) and showed both her jumping ability and front-running intent with a win and two seconds in recent starts; the STYLE_FIT flag is a reminder she performs best when she dictates, and with no rival likely to challenge for the lead, conditions here suit her perfectly.

runners_data.name: Miss Fedora
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield's seven-year-old is running in her second race within 10 days, has the headgear note of a hood, and her last five completed starts on good ground produced just one win and one place from nine qualifying runs — she is a genuine hold-up type whose true race position will be further back than the map indicates, and the quick turnaround and low OR-75 are concerns.

races.paceDynamic: Northern Rose is the sole confirmed front runner and, with no rival willing or able to press her hard, she will stride into an uncontested lead from the outset and dictate a controlled, honest gallop on good ground over two and a half miles. The five hold-up types — Jammy Jay, Prettylady, I Heard A Rumour, Daring To Dream and Miss Fedora — will be settled in behind her, meaning the race resolves into a straightforward test of who can pick up most effectively from the home turn. I Heard A Rumour, Daring To Dream and Miss Fedora are genuine hold-up horses who have been mapped to midfield simply because this field has more true rear-runners than the pace map has room to accommodate; in reality they will all try to settle further back than their mapped positions suggest, and Northern Rose is almost certain to secure her lead unchallenged. This shape — a single uncontested pace-setter, a patient chasing pack, and a decisive late run — heavily favours a prominent-to-lead profile that can control the tempo and deny the closers a target to aim at, or alternatively a horse with enough class to quicken from a handy position without needing a true end-to-end gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Northern Rose Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Northern Rose jumps fluently and maintains her uncontested lead throughout at a comfortable gallop.
scenarios.body: Northern Rose dictates every yard at a sustainable clip, jumps accurately enough to keep her rivals at bay, and turns the race into an endurance test of who can sustain momentum to the line; her good-ground record (15 runs all on good, 1W 8P) underlines she is entirely at home in these conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Northern Rose is just brisk enough to leave her vulnerable in the final flight.
scenarios.body: A slightly stronger gallop than anticipated drains enough from Northern Rose that a quality hold-up horse can sweep past on the run-in; the horse who has settled deepest and widest can produce the best late kick on a fresh, good surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prettylady Pings Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Prettylady jumps boldly from the front of the chasing group and strikes for home turning in.
scenarios.body: Despite being a hold-up type, Prettylady's recent sharp winning form (two consecutive wins) at this sort of trip gives her the tactical speed to move into a prominent pitch at a crucial moment and outbattle rivals; the tongue tie and her trainer's in-form yard (1/7 over 14 days) add small but real angles.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Moderate Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Northern Rose's gallop is so slow that the race turns into a sprint finish from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A crawl-and-sprint test suits a horse with raw speed rather than staying resolution, but with this field full of true hold-up mares who will be bunched and shuffled at a slow pace, the outcome becomes chaotic and difficult to predict; this scenario is least likely precisely because Northern Rose's recent form shows consistent front-running and she has no incentive to dawdle.

watchPoints.text: Northern Rose's jumping accuracy is the critical variable — watch her at the early hurdles because a mistake could hand the pace to no-one and completely unsettle the race shape.
I Heard A Rumour has been off 171 days and has a fall on her recent form; watch for signs of rustiness or jumping errors that could compromise Skelton's hope of a smooth reintroduction.
Prettylady is the most likely beneficiary if Northern Rose weakens — watch her position rounding the home turn, as a forward move from her natural tracking spot would signal her chance.

With three true hold-up horses (I Heard A Rumour, Daring To Dream, Miss Fedora) all manoeuvring for rear positions, watch for traffic congestion down the back and at the home turn as they all try to settle outside one another.

Jammy Jay's rider Ben Poste will need to balance not getting too far back against not getting into a speed battle with Northern Rose — watch her position at halfway as a guide to whether she is travelling within herself.

races.name: Lexus Wrexham Open 2026 Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Harrys Hope
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Ben Pauling with an excellent Good-ground profile (11 runs, 3 wins, 9 places on similar going), consistent placer over this 23f trip range, only 16 days since last run so fitness assured; tongue-tie applied, and this race shape — honest pace to chase down — suits his profile squarely.

runners_data.name: Post Chaise
runners_data.note: Returns from a massive 554-day absence for Greenall & Guerriero, which is the defining unknown here; placed record on Soft historically but has limited Good-ground form (1 win from 3 placed runs), and Toby Wynne will need to produce a race-fit performance from a cold reappearance — treat with caution until fitness is proven.

runners_data.name: Ridin Solo
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for Donald McCain, three recent placings over 20f on Good and Soft, though winless in recent starts (0W3P on similar going in last 12 runs); 83 days off is manageable, and Theo Gillard will look to utilise a pressing position to grind out a staying performance.

runners_data.name: Back In The Bay
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for James Owen with a dominant Good-ground record (10 of 11 runs on similar going, 2 wins, 5 places); Jonathan Burke will look to dictate from the front and his 16-day turnaround indicates he's in a productive vein — the danger is Limerick Leader pushing him into a pace battle that costs late.

runners_data.name: Depalma
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for the high-powered Harry Skelton and Dan Skelton combination (T14: 9/21 — strong recent form), but limited Good-ground form at this trip range with no wins or placings on similar going in last 10 relevant runs; 110 days off is the longest absence in the field and a concern, though Skelton can produce a patient tactical ride if the pace fully suits.

runners_data.name: Limerick Leader
runners_data.note: Second confirmed front-runner for James Bowen and Nick Scholfield, boasting an outstanding Good-ground record (12 of 15 runs, 2 wins, 10 places on similar going) and a series of consistent placings; tongue-bar noted, and the crucial issue is whether contesting the lead with Back In The Bay costs him late on this stamina-testing 3m circuit.

runners_data.name: Royal Time
runners_data.note: Naturally a hold-up horse for Jack Tudor and Christian Williams, but pushed into an artificial midfield position on the pace map because the field is saturated with rearward types — his true style will see him settle towards the back; a U (unseated) features in recent form and he is 106 days off, adding further uncertainty to an already compromised tactical position.

runners_data.name: Bahtiyar
runners_data.note: Strong Good-ground handler (15 of 15 relevant runs on similar going) for Ben Poste and Max Young, but his natural hold-up style is similarly displaced on the pace map by an abundance of hold-up runners in this field — he'll likely settle at the rear of his own accord; lightly raced trainer (T14: 0/1) and an OR of 75 underscores he is well below the class ceiling of the leading contenders here.

races.paceDynamic: Back In The Bay and Limerick Leader are confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 3m trip at Bangor, creating a genuine, honest gallop on Good ground — neither is likely to yield willingly. This contested early pace over an extended trip should stretch the field and put a premium on stamina and jumping accuracy in the closing stages. Post Chaise and Ridin Solo will look to press from prominent positions, compressing the early order further and ensuring no let-up. This race shape distinctly favours proven stayers who can travel within themselves in midfield or just off the pace and produce a sustained challenge from the home turn — a hold-up or patient-prominent profile suits best, provided it is genuine rather than artificial. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Back In The Bay is best-placed to lead given Jonathan Burke's forceful front-running style, while Limerick Leader is likeliest to push hardest for the rail, leaving Post Chaise and Ridin Solo shuffled slightly wider and fractionally further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Stayer Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Back In The Bay and Limerick Leader fight for supremacy and sustain an honest gallop that stretches the field throughout the 3m trip.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other up over the fences, leaving an advantaged position for a horse who has tracked at a comfortable distance before unleashing a staying run from the final turn; Harrys Hope's strong Good-ground form and consistent placed record over this trip profile make it a prime beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pacemakers — most likely Back In The Bay — asserts early and Limerick Leader is unable to sustain the challenge, leaving a solo front-runner to control tempo.
scenarios.body: A solo leader on Good ground over 3m at Bangor can dictate a measured gallop and conserve enough in reserve to hold on jumping the final fences; Back In The Bay's excellent Good-going record (10/11 runs) and recent winning form over course-appropriate trips makes it the biggest threat in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Hold-Up Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the front-running battle is truly gruelling and a genuine hold-up horse finds clear daylight late to swoop on weary leaders.
scenarios.body: Depalma, tracking wide off the pace for Harry Skelton, represents the most credible version of this shape given Skelton's tactical acumen, though Good ground may not fully play to his strengths based on historic form; Royal Time and Bahtiyar are natural hold-up types but are mapped artificially forward in this shape, reducing the reliability of this scenario materially.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Player Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and a prominent racer who settles just behind the leaders proves to have the superior stamina reserves to pick off a tiring field.
scenarios.body: Ridin Solo, consistent in placing over 20f on Good ground under Theo Gillard for Donald McCain, could prove the surprise beneficiary if the race fragments and positional advantage counts for more than raw class; Post Chaise, returning from 554 days off, carries the biggest unknown in the field and could outperform a cold market if fitness is spot on.

watchPoints.text: Back In The Bay and Limerick Leader — watch whether either blinks before halfway; if both are still fighting for the lead at the 2m mark, neither may have enough in reserve to repel late challengers.

Post Chaise — 554 days off is a significant fitness risk; watch for signs of greenness or fading after the second-last fence which would confirm this is a reintroduction run rather than a winning return.

Depalma — Harry Skelton tends to maximise hold-up types tactically, but watch where he positions from the start; if he is forced wide or further back than planned, the Bangor home straight may be too short for a meaningful late run.

Royal Time — watch where Jack Tudor actually settles in the early stages; if he rides him closer than his natural hold-up profile suggests, it may indicate stable confidence in fitness after 106 days off and worth noting for the market.

Harrys Hope — Ben Jones will be aiming to track the leaders at a controlled distance; watch his position at the cross fence on the final circuit as his jumping accuracy at that point has historically been a reliable indicator of his chance.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Bobby Socks
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner here; Quinlan can dictate every yard on Good ground she handles well, but her last win was 83 days ago over a trip shorter than today's and this mark of OR 100 at 168lbs is her ceiling — her stamina under top weight is the key question.

runners_data.name: Faded Fantasy
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse for Christian Williams whose trainer has gone 0 from 5 in the last 14 days; last five runs show a consistent tendency to finish mid-division in similar fields, and the controlled pace here won't generate the late surge she needs.

runners_data.name: Present Fair
runners_data.note: McCain's nine-year-old won off OR-equivalent ground at Bangor before but has been beaten out of sight in her last two Good-ground outings; Mr Harry Brown's 10lb claim is a meaningful weight relief, yet her recent form string of 0105-7 reads erratically.

runners_data.name: La Lolita
runners_data.note: Only 12 days since her last run and a course-suitable five-year-old for Gary Hanmer who handles Good ground exceptionally well — 9/10 in similar conditions — and James Bowen gives her every chance of positioning handily close to the pace where this race will be decided.

runners_data.name: Eyeeye
runners_data.note: Carries a ⚠ fade flag in the finish and is a true hold-up horse whose last five runs show a string of poor finishes on Good ground; the redistribution into midfield reflects the overcrowded rear of this field, but fading in the closing stages undermines any chance even if she settles better than expected.

runners_data.name: Ballynoe Boy
runners_data.note: Won last time out at 18f on Good ground and has the profile of a horse that could press the pace; his true hold-up style means he's unlikely to get that position in a field this stacked, but recent winning form and Danny McMenamin's positive booking make him one of the more interesting behind-the-scenes chances.

runners_data.name: Ashdown Forest
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's four-year-old is the freshest page in the race in terms of age, and Harry Skelton's booking alongside a T14 record of 9/21 is the strongest trainer-jockey combination on the card; stepped up from 16f wins, the 19f trip stretches him but Good ground suits and he's the most natural prominent-tracking candidate behind Bobby Socks.

runners_data.name: Lord Cauvelliere
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type for Sheila Lewis who has run 8 of his last 8 races on Good ground — all without winning; the blinkers are a new addition but his form string of 77-456 at 16-17f distances shorter than today's does not inspire confidence at this trip.

runners_data.name: Cappa Lass
runners_data.note: 111 days off the track is a notable absence for this five-year-old, and her sole three form runs on Good ground have all produced placed-or-worse finishes in the 6-8 range; the hood headgear and Jack Tudor's booking are minor positives but she needs this run to fire.

runners_data.name: Cawthorne Cracker
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has run 13 of 15 career starts on Good ground and shown genuine consistency in placing (1W6P), wearing tongue-strap and cheekpieces; his form at 17f is better than the current 19f trip suggests and he'll need a well-run race to get competitive late.

runners_data.name: Dante's Inferno
runners_data.note: Tony Culhane's seven-year-old hasn't run in 111 days and his last five runs on Good ground all ended in the 3-7 range without a win; Jonathan Burke is a quality booking but a horse with 0 wins from 10 Good-ground runs since his last success is hard to upgrade sharply.

runners_data.name: Lucky In Taipan
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's six-year-old arrives off a 16-day turnaround with a T14 strike-rate of 3/6 — the yard is in form — and his recent 3rd at 20f on Good ground is the most relevant piece of positive evidence; at OR 72 with 142lbs he has the lightest burden in the field, which may compensate for his hold-up style in a slowly-run race.

races.paceDynamic: Bobby Socks is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival — she can slide into a rhythm from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m3½f at Bangor. With the tempo entirely in her own hands and Sean Quinlan able to dictate every surge and settle, the race is set up for a patient lead that turns into a punishing test of stamina from the home turn rather than a flat-out burn from the off. The field behind her is dominated by hold-up types, but the sheer volume of them means several — most notably Eyeeye, Ballynoe Boy, and Lord Cauvelliere — cannot all race as deep closers and will be pushed closer to the pace than they would naturally choose. This shape overwhelmingly favours horses that can travel prominently or just off the lone front-runner and produce a sustained gallop through the closing stages, rather than those relying on a late sprint off a genuinely strong pace that simply will not materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If Bobby Socks dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the field is strung out by the final circuit, rewarding those who travel closest.
scenarios.body: Bobby Socks controls tempo from the front and the race becomes a test of jumping fluency and staying power in the final half-mile; horses that can sit in her slipstream and produce a clean round of jumping hold every advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or early-tracking horse holds a perfect position off Bobby Socks and picks her off approaching the last.
scenarios.body: A horse like Ashdown Forest or La Lolita, racing in the first three from an early stage, conserves enough energy to mount a sustained challenge on the run-in; the lone pace-setter eventually tires in the closing stages and is run down by a fresher, well-positioned rival.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically or a field incident causes carnage, gifting ground to a deep closer.
scenarios.body: One of the redistributed hold-up horses — most likely Ballynoe Boy or Faded Fantasy — benefits from a chaotic mid-race incident or an unusually sharp injection of pace that sees front-runners capitulate; the true late-runner storms home but needs things to go badly wrong for the prominent horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Falls Back
scenarios.trigger: If Bobby Socks makes a significant jumping error or is headed unexpectedly, creating a tactical vacuum and a bunched finish.
scenarios.body: Without any horse willing to take up the running, the field crawls and the race turns into a sprint from the second-last, suiting a quick-ground flat-track type with a turn of foot; this shape is the least likely given Bobby Socks's proven front-running profile.

watchPoints.text: Bobby Socks holds the entire tempo in her hands — if she ping-jumps from the front and Sean Quinlan settles her into a rhythm, this race is hers to lose, and any bettor must monitor whether she's allowed to stride clear unchallenged on the home turn.

Ashdown Forest is the one horse whose profile most naturally threatens Bobby Socks — watch whether Harry Skelton positions him in the first three early; if he does, the Skelton yard's 9/21 T14 form makes him the most dangerous pursuer.

La Lolita ran just 12 days ago and James Bowen may attempt to hold a prominent pitch from flag fall — if she tracks the leader from the outset, she becomes a live player in Scenario A and B, but a repeat of her recent 4th and 5th finishes would confirm she needs stronger pace.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Eyeeye, Ballynoe Boy, Lord Cauvelliere, Cappa Lass, Cawthorne Cracker, Dante's Inferno, Lucky In Taipan — will jostle for midfield positions they don't naturally want; watch for crowding and interference at hurdles on the far side in the opening mile.

Lucky In Taipan's trainer Ben Pauling is 3/6 in the last 14 days — the yard is firing — and at the bottom of the weights (142lbs, OR 72) he represents the each-way price watch, particularly if the pace is slow enough for a hold-up horse to get competitive without needing a true strong gallop.
